text.p: Shareholders of French insurers Axa and UAP Monday overwhelmingly approved the megamerger of the two companies, creating the second-largest insurer in the world.
The vote, at a shareholder's meeting, eliminated the last legal hurdle to the two companies' alliance, carried out through a stock swap.
"It's very encouraging," Claude Bebear, chief executive of the new group, told reporters. "Now we must get down to work to complete the synergies which we said would happen."
Over the past two decades, Bebear has guided Axa from a sleepy French mutual insurance company into an acquisitive powerhouse.
The companies surprised financial markets last November by announcing they would combine operations to form a group with combined revenues of 340 billion francs ($59.8 billion).

They have been integrating their operations since the announcement of the deal, initially valued at around at 40 billion francs ($7 billion) but now reported to be worth close to 50 billion ($8.8 billion).

While Axa and UAP called the operation a merger, financial analysts said it was clear that it was more a friendly takeover by strongly profitable Axa of UAP, which had been hard hit by the French property slump.
The holding company will be known as Axa-UAP while the brand name worldwide will be Axa. Axa now holds 91.39 percent of UAP shares.
Bebear reiterated that the company was aiming for a return on equity of 11 percent from 1998 and 15 percent by the year 2001 or 2002, up from 10.2 percent in 1996.
Separately, Axa-UAP reported first quarter consolidated revenues rose 11.0 percent to 98.66 billion francs ($17.4 billion) from 88.92 billion ($15.7 billion). Revenues rose 6.1 percent.
